title: Past Tense ED Endings (/t/, /d/, /ɪd/)
objectives: Apply the three past tense -ed ending sounds
Add extra syllable /ɪd/ only after T and D
Prevent unwanted extra syllables on /t/ and /d/ endings

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner pronounces 'walked' as /wɔːkɪd/ (2 syllables).
💡 Solution: Tap rhythm: 'walk' (1 tap) -> 'walked' (1 tap, ending with /t/ snap).

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Past Tense ED Endings (/t/, /d/, /ɪd/)
1. Definition: Regular past tense suffix -ed has three pronunciations conditioned by the root's final sound.
2. Rule: 1. After voiceless (/p, k, f, s, ʃ, tʃ/) = /t/ (walked). 2. After voiced (vowels, /b, g, v, z, m, n, l, r/) = /d/ (called). 3. After /t/ or /d/ = /ɪd/ (wanted, needed).
3. Why? Voice assimilation prevents awkward tongue shifts.
4. How to recognize? Check the last sound of the base verb before adding -ed.
5. Common examples: walked /wɔːkt/, jumped /dʒʌmpt/, called /kɔːld/, played /pleɪd/, wanted /ˈwɒntɪd/, needed /ˈniːdɪd/
6. Counter-examples: Irregular verbs (went, saw, came).
7. Exceptions: Adjectives ending in -ed sometimes pronounce /ɪd/ (learned, naked, wicked).
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing 'walked' as 2 syllables (*walk-ed) instead of 1 syllable (/wɔːkt/).
9. Mnemonic / Hint: ONLY /t/ and /d/ base verbs get an extra syllable /ɪd/!
10. Key vocabulary: past tense -ed, extra syllable, voiceless /t/, voiced /d/, syllabic /ɪd/
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟢 A1
13. Associated Visual: ➕ Extra syllable box only for T and D verbs.
14. Key Takeaway: T/D base = /ɪd/ extra syllable! Unvoiced = /t/, Voiced = /d/.

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: How many syllables are in 'walked'? (1 syllable: /wɔːkt/)
CCQ 2: When does -ed add an extra syllable /ɪd/? (Only when the base verb ends in T or D)
CCQ 3: How is -ed pronounced in 'called'? (/d/)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Count syllables and identify the -ed sound:
🎯 Item: walked ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: 1 syllable -> /t/
🎯 Item: played ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: 1 syllable -> /d/
🎯 Item: wanted ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: 2 syllables -> /ɪd/
